o1.biggest_strength: It makes the right call against the 20% cut with the lifetime maths, then focuses the plan on the top creator-educator partners and the credit-window/payout fixes.
o1.biggest_mistake: The Day 30 payout item is a bit too neat operationally, since a 30-days-after-month-end payout schedule may not produce a real first payout within the first 30 days.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a small day-90 scorecard and tighten the payout transition timing so finance and the partner manager can run it without interpretation.

o2.biggest_strength: It clearly proves why the 20% cut is risky and gives a strong 90-day window, payout, rules and review plan.
o2.biggest_mistake: The 40% Partner tier and free accounts add cost and complexity that are not fully controlled inside the $40,000 perk budget or the one-manager constraint.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Keep the Partner tier reward mostly in managed perks and service, or cap the 40% tier tightly with a clearer cost ceiling and eligibility limit.

reason: Output 1 is the plan I would rather hand to the team tomorrow: it is sharper on the top-20 focus, keeps costs simpler, and fixes the tracking and payout problems without creating a new commission-risk layer. Output 2 is strong, but the 40% Partner tier makes the finance conversation harder than it needs to be.
